Hi everyone, I'm Siddharth; I work in automorphic forms and the (relative) Langlands program. I'm currently finishing my PhD at Boston College.
I've been interested in Lean and mathlib for a long time, but I've only recently started to learn it seriously. I'm interested in contributing to parts of mathlib related to local and global representation theory.
Once I have more experience under my belt, I'd really like to work towards formalizing the Arthur-Selberg trace formula, beginning with the special case of anisotropic groups. There are so many inputs that go into this, and I'd love to hear your thoughts about what the first steps might be.
My first instinct would be to focus on anisotropic G which admit an integral model over Z (so are split at all finite places and compact at infinity) and try and topologize G(Z_p) < G(Q_p), G(R) and G(A) (for A the adeles over Q) and formalize how the topology on the adelic points is related to the topology at the local places. Does this sound reasonable?
If there are already people thinking about this/working on this, I'd love to connect and chat more!
Thanks, I look forward to meeting you all :)

We have things like this in the special case where G is the units of a central simple algebra in the FLT repo. The issue with doing it in general is that we should really decide how to say "connected reductive group" first (we already know how to say "units of a central simple algebra" so this is why I could make progress there already).

Is there a document/post where this is being discussed? I found a lot of scattered discussion on zulip and in the FLT blueprint, but no clear plan. Maybe more relevant, is there some useful way that a beginner to Lean could contribute?

I'm currently working on formalizing the classification of subgroups of G_a over a field, mostly to get some practice with Lean, but also with some vague thought that this might be useful to relate various (eventual) definitions of unipotent group...

Well, "how to formalize the definition of a connected reductive group" is an open problem in the area right now :-/ The way to say "let G be an affine algebraic group (of finite type) over Q" is perhaps something like this

import Mathlib

open CategoryTheory AlgebraicGeometry

-- let G be an affine group scheme of finite type over ℚ
variable (G : Scheme) (φ : G ⟶ Spec <| CommRingCat.of ℚ)
  [GrpObj (Over.mk φ)] [IsAffine G] [LocallyOfFiniteType φ]

but for "reductive" we will ideally need the Hopf algebra and I think we're still waiting for stuff from the Toric variety project to be upstreamed? Not sure what the state of the art is. How are you defining G_a over a field? Using the Hopf algebra or using the scheme?

I was using Hopf algebras, just for simplicity. The classification just boils down to proving that all monic additive polynomials have the form f(T) = \sum a_i T^{p^i} when the field has char p, which I should (hopefully!) have done soon :)
